item.subject: science
item.stem: Meera's teacher asks her to explain why the broad, flat leaves of the money plant growing near her classroom window are good at making food. Which answer correctly justifies this?

options.A: Broad, flat leaves give a large surface to receive sunlight, so the chlorophyll in the leaf can make more food by photosynthesis.
options.B: Broad, flat leaves can make food even in complete darkness, because their shape alone is enough for photosynthesis.
options.C: Broad, flat leaves spread the sunlight more thinly, so they make less food than narrow leaves under the same light.
options.D: Broad, flat leaves capture more sunlight so that they can carry out respiration, which makes food for the plant.
